Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 15.09.2011 passed in MVC No.7364/2010 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -V, Court of Small Causes at Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'),
the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 22.10.2010, at about 8.30 a.m., near Nagappa Street, the petitioner was proceeding on motor cycle bearing registration No.KA.02.EE.2320 at that time a Maruthi Wagon R car bearing registration No.KA.04.MH.6071, which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner and duly insured with respondent No.2 - Insurance Company, because of the said accident, the petitioner suffered the following injuries:
i. Montaggia Fracture dislocation of left forearm.
4. The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.97,600/- along with interest @ 8% p.a. under the following heads:-
SL.NO. HEADS OF COMPENSATION AMOUNT IN RS.
1. Pain and suffering 30,000 2.
Medical and incidental expenses 50,000 3.
Future medical expenses 10,000 4.
Loss of income during the laid up 7,000 period 5.
Loss of amenities in life 25,000 Total 1,22,000
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 5. Admittedly, the accident happened in the year 2010.
The petitioner was aged 27 years at the time of accident and he sustained whole body disability of 6% as per the evidence of the doctor.
There is no reason to disbelieve the same.
The petitioner has failed to establish his income before the Tribunal.
Thus, his notional income as per lok adalath chart is taken at Rs.5,500/- per month.
Given his age, the multiplier of 17 has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. D.T.C [2009(6) SCC 121].
Thus, towards 'loss of future income' the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.67,320/- (Rs.5,500 x 12x 17 x 6%).
Given the nature of injuries, 3 months is considered to be the laid up period and the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.16,500/- (5,500 x 3) as against Rs.7,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Towards the head pain and suffering, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/-.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards the head 'Medical expenses', based on the medical bills, a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards the head 'loss of amenities', a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded, which I deem it appropriate.
Towards future medical expenses, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
6. Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads is modified as hereunder:-
